subject: Materials Science
title: Sports Equipment: Lighter, Faster
description: A quick, practical guide to Sports Equipment: Lighter, Faster.

hook.text: A carbon fiber tennis racket weighs 250 grams yet withstands impacts that would bend aluminum.

buildup.text: Composites let designers tune stiffness and damping — stiffer shafts for power, flexible for feel.

discovery.text: Bicycle frames, ski poles, hockey sticks, and rowing oars are almost entirely carbon composite.

twist.text: The same properties that prevent bending also mean catastrophic failure — composites snap, not dent.

climax.text: Olympic records keep falling partly because equipment keeps getting lighter and stiffer.

punchline.text: Lighter gear doesn't make the athlete — but it helps the records fall.

quiz.question: What is a risk of using composites in sports equipment?
options: They are too heavy for competition
They fail suddenly by snapping rather than denting
They lose stiffness after one use
